title: Italy taken to decider again in Davis Cup semifinal
description: Italy faces a deciding doubles match in the Davis Cup semifinal after the Czech Republic tied the series at 1-1. A win is crucial for Italy’s hopes of securing a fourth consecutive title.
text: BOLOGNA, Italy: Lorenzo Musetti pulled off an impressive double duty, triumphing in both singles and doubles to send Italy into a fourth consecutive Davis Cup final at the expense of Czech Republic on Friday in Bologna.
Just as he did against South Korea three days ago, Musetti opened the scoring for the hosts, defeating Jakub Mensik 6-3, 6-4 for what he described as “the biggest victory of my career in Davis Cup.”
Flavio Cobolli then suffered his second loss of the week, falling 6-2, 1-6, 6-3 to an in-form Jiri Lehecka as the semifinal tie went to a deciding doubles.

Musetti then returned to the court to team up with doubles specialist Andrea Vavassori for a 3-6, 6-1, 7-6 (7/4) win over Lehecka and Tomas Machac that earned the Italians a 16th consecutive tie victory in the Davis Cup.
Italy are only the second nation in the post-Challenge Round era to make four finals in a row, after Sweden, who reached seven consecutive finals from 1983 to 1989.
They now await Spain or Great Britain in Sunday’s final.

“This has a special meaning in my heart, especially because my last matches in the Davis Cup weren’t wins, so I felt that I needed this to come back and to prove that I could help the team,” said Musetti, whose voice was hoarse from screaming throughout the match.
“So today, finally, I think I showed that I can, that I’m there and that I really care about the team, and I’m really, really happy to be sharing the court with Andrea.
“We are such good friends, and I’m really happy for everything he’s achieved. So for me, was really amazing.”
Vavassori, ranked No.10 in doubles, took the opportunity to take aim at the ATP, who have taken decisions to scale back on doubles competitions and redirect prize money from doubles to singles.
“I’m so happy because winning like this is the best feeling ever,” he said.

“And I really think that ATP management has to see these matches because I think doubles is really entertaining, and here is the proof because we did so many emotions, and in Davis Cup, it’s the best feeling.”

Musetti, a former world number five who is down to 27 in the rankings, missed two and half months of action that forced him out of the French Open and Wimbledon earlier this season but is enjoying a strong end to his 2026 campaign, with a title picked up in Lyon last month, followed by a semifinal run in Stockholm.

Mensik, who didn’t play in the Czech Republic’s 2-0 quarter-final victory over Canada on Tuesday, fired 13 aces but struggled on his second serve, winning just 25 percent of the points behind his second delivery.

“It feels amazing, honestly. I knew that Jakub was a really tough player, especially on this surface, serving bombs from the beginning,” said Musetti, who saved all six break points he faced during the match.
The seventh-ranked Cobolli shone for Italy last year, claiming three victories in as many matches to help the hosts secure the Davis Cup title in Bologna.
But his fortunes have turned this time around, as he lost to Kwon Soonwoo in the quarter-finals against South Korea before his defeat to Lehecka on Friday.
